technical_and_design_decisions: Global DSL timeout and pollInterval options will be implemented as top-level configuration properties in the Spring Integration DSL, with local component-level overrides taking precedence over global values.
The Spring Integration 4.2.1 upgrade will maintain backward compatibility with all existing public APIs used by the project, with deprecated API usages updated to their recommended replacements.

JobLaunchingTasklet refactoring will prioritize non-breaking changes to the public interface of the tasklet, with performance improvements validated via standardized benchmark tests against the original implementation.

Inline SpEL expressions in stream definitions will be evaluated at stream initialization time, with support for accessing message payload, headers, and predefined environment variables as expression context.
The new undeployed YARN SPI status will be added as a distinct enum value, with all existing logic that relied on the unknown state for undeployed YARN applications updated to use the new status.

The admin artifact split will follow a modular structure, with a core admin module containing shared logic and separate, optional modules for each supported Hadoop distribution version, to minimize dependency bloat for users.

Test coverage enhancements will target 90% line coverage for DSL and XML generation code paths, with test cases covering all valid configuration variants, invalid input handling, and custom module integration scenarios.
Job orchestration documentation will include runnable code samples compatible with the project's current supported Spring Integration version, to ensure examples work out of the box for users.
assumptions: The development team has existing expertise in Spring Integration, Spring DSL, YARN integration, and the project's build tooling (Maven/Gradle), eliminating the need for extensive onboarding.
Full access to the project's source code repository, CI/CD pipeline, test environments, and YARN cluster test resources is available throughout the development period.

The Spring Integration 4.2.1 upgrade does not introduce breaking changes to any public APIs used by the project, and all required dependency versions are available in the project's internal artifact repository.

The current unknown YARN SPI status is exclusively associated with undeployed YARN applications, so replacing it with the undeployed status will not cause unintended side effects in other system components.
The project's existing test suite is fully functional and can be extended to cover the new requirements without requiring significant rework of existing test infrastructure.
Only two major Hadoop distribution versions (e.g., Hadoop 2.x and 3.x) require separate admin artifact modules, to keep the artifact structure maintainable.

No additional external dependencies are required to implement the inline SpEL expression support for stream definitions, as the required SpEL libraries are already included in the project's dependency tree.
